title: Implement async scheduler with ready queue and WASI poll bridge
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 0
- labels: runtime,async,parallelism
- description: |
    The async scheduler is currently all stubs (camp_async_init/enqueue/dequeue/run are no-ops). Without a working scheduler, any program using Async! traps at runtime. This is the single biggest blocker for real-world async/concurrent programs.
- design: |
    Per openspec/specs/parallelism/design.md:
    1. Ready Queue: FIFO of coroutine closures ready to run
    2. Blocked Map: WASI pollable → waiting coroutines
    3. Handle Table: handle_id → {status, result} for structured concurrency
    4. Join Waiters: handle_id → coroutines waiting on join!
    5. Scheduler loop: dequeue → resume → handle completion/block/yield → poll if idle
    6. WASI poll bridge: subscribe to pollables, move ready coroutines to queue
    7. Time.sleep! via poll timeout
- acceptance: Async programs with spawn/join/yield run end-to-end; I/O operations block and resume correctly

title: Implement closure serialization for multi-instance parallelism
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 0
- labels: runtime,parallelism
- description: |
    Multi-instance parallelism (Spawn!/Parallel! with thread handlers) requires serializing closures across WASM instances. Currently not implemented. Without this, Spawn! and Parallel! can only use the sequential handler.
- design: |
    Per openspec/specs/parallelism/design.md §Closure Serialization:
    1. Serialized format: magic(0x4350) + version(1) + fn_index + env_size + env_bytes + effect_row_bitmask
    2. Deep copy strings/lists into closure env (cannot pass by pointer across instances)
    3. Worker deserializes into its own heap
    4. Effect row bitmask tells worker which handlers to install
- acceptance: Closures can be serialized, sent to worker instances, deserialized, and executed

title: Implement thread pool manager for multi-instance parallelism
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 0
- labels: runtime,parallelism
- description: |
    The thread pool manager (MPMC work queue, result map, worker threads) is not implemented. This is the host-side infrastructure that runs in the Camp CLI (Odin), not in WASM. Required for Spawn!/Parallel! with thread handlers.
- design: |
    Per openspec/specs/parallelism/design.md §Multi-Instance Architecture:
    1. Thread Pool Manager: MPMC channel for work items, thread-safe result map
    2. Worker loop: dequeue → instantiate WASM → run_task → store result
    3. Join blocking: host callback blocks OS thread until result available
    4. Chunk-based work distribution for Parallel.map!
    5. Error propagation: serialize thrown tags back to main instance
- acceptance: Spawn.spawn! submits work to thread pool; Spawn.join! blocks until result available

title: Throw default handler must render tag to stderr
description:
- type: bug
- priority: 1
- labels: effects,codegen,runtime
- description: |
    The effects spec requires that the default Throw! handler renders the unhandled tag to stderr before exiting with code 1. Currently `emit_throw_handler_fn` in codegen.odin just calls `camp_exit(1)` without reading or printing the thrown tag value. The `err` parameter (i32) is available but unused.
- design: |
    1. In `emit_throw_handler_fn`, before calling `camp_exit(1)`: load the err parameter, use `RUNTIME_PRINT_ERR` to print "unhandled: " prefix, then print the tag value
    2. May need a runtime function to convert i32 tag to string or just print the raw value
- acceptance: Default Throw handler prints tag info to stderr before exiting

title: par {} should return tuple, not List
description:
- type: bug
- priority: 1
- labels: canonicalize,parallelism
- description: |
    The parallelism spec says `par { e1, e2, e3 }` returns a tuple `(T1, T2, T3)` preserving individual types. The current implementation desugars to `Parallel!.all!([|| e1, || e2, || e3])` which returns `List(a)` — losing type information and requiring all expressions to have the same type.
- design: |
    1. Add tuple expression support to the AST (Expr_Tuple, CExpr_Tuple, TExpr_Tuple)
    2. Change par {} desugaring to construct a tuple instead of a list
    3. Each element gets its own type variable, preserving the individual types
- acceptance: par { e1, e2 } returns (T1, T2) with distinct types per expression

title: IR_Drop_Reuse and IR_Alloc_At codegen (Perceus in-place reuse)
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 1
- labels: codegen,rc
- description: |
    `IR_Drop_Reuse` and `IR_Alloc_At` both emit `Wasm_Unreachable` in codegen. These are needed for Perceus reference counting to reuse memory in-place instead of always allocating fresh. Without them, the compiler always allocates new heap objects even when old ones could be reused.
- design: |
    1. IR_Drop_Reuse: decrement refcount, if zero reuse the memory slot for next allocation
    2. IR_Alloc_At: allocate at a specific memory address (for in-place construction)
    3. Both need careful WASM memory management integration with camp_alloc/camp_dealloc
- acceptance: Programs using in-place reuse don't trap; memory reuse reduces allocation count

title: Implement string runtime (concat, slice, len, eq)
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 1
- labels: runtime
- description: |
    String runtime is incomplete: camp_str_len and camp_str_eq are simplistic; camp_str_concat and camp_str_slice don't exist. Strings are fundamental to I/O and user-facing programs.
- design: |
    1. camp_str_concat: allocate new string, copy both, return pointer
    2. camp_str_slice: allocate substring, copy range, return pointer
    3. camp_str_len: read length from string header (first i32)
    4. camp_str_eq: compare lengths, then byte-by-byte comparison
    5. Perceus RC: dup/drop string references
- acceptance: String concat/slice/len/eq work correctly; RC is correct

title: Implement list runtime with growth and bounds checking
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 1
- labels: runtime
- description: |
    The list runtime (camp_list_alloc/push/len/get) is naive: no capacity growth, no bounds checking, no Perceus RC integration. Lists are fundamental to most programs.
- design: |
    1. camp_list_push: check capacity, grow if needed (double capacity, realloc)
    2. camp_list_get: bounds check, trap on out-of-range
    3. Perceus RC: dup/drop list references, decrement element refcounts on drop
    4. camp_list_concat: efficient append
- acceptance: Lists grow dynamically; out-of-bounds access traps; RC is correct

title: Effect polymorphism missing on Parallel operations
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 1
- labels: typecheck,effects,parallelism
- description: |
    Parallel! operations should propagate the inner function's effects through effect polymorphism. For example, `map! : <a, b, e>|items: List(a), f: |a| -[e]-> b| -[Parallel! | e]-> List(b)`. Currently `effect_ops[parallel_name]` has `param_types = nil` — no effect variable propagation through callbacks.
- design: |
    1. Add effect row variables to Parallel! operation signatures in inject_prelude
    2. When typechecking a Parallel! perform call, extract the callback's effect row and compose with Parallel!
    3. This requires the effect polymorphism infrastructure from Group 10 to work for prelude effects
- acceptance: Functions passed to par_map! can have custom effects that propagate to caller

title: Implement for loop syntax
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: parser,canonicalize
- description: |
    `Kw_For` exists in the token enum but there's no `for x in xs { body }` parsing. The `par for` variant works but plain `for` doesn't.
- design: |
    1. Parse `for x in xs { body }` in parser_parse_prefix
    2. Desugar to `xs.iter().for_each(|x| body)` or equivalent recursive function
- acceptance: `for x in xs { body }` parses and desugars correctly

title: Implement atomic WASM opcodes in codegen
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: codegen,parallelism
- description: |
    All six atomic IR nodes (IR_Atomic_Load, IR_Atomic_Store, IR_Atomic_RMW, IR_Atomic_Fence, IR_Wait, IR_Notify) emit Wasm_Unreachable in codegen. The actual WASM atomic opcodes (0xFE prefix) need to be emitted.
- design: |
    Per openspec/specs/parallelism/design.md §WASM Threads:
    1. IR_Atomic_Load{.B4}: emit 0xFE 0x10 + alignment + offset
    2. IR_Atomic_Store{.B4}: emit 0xFE 0x17 + alignment + offset
    3. IR_Atomic_RMW{.Add, .B4}: emit 0xFE 0x1E + alignment + offset
    4. IR_Atomic_RMW{.CmpXchg, .B4}: emit 0xFE 0x48 + alignment + offset
    5. IR_Atomic_Fence: emit 0xFE 0x50
    6. IR_Wait{.B4}: emit 0xFE 0x52 + alignment + offset
    7. IR_Notify: emit 0xFE 0x54 + alignment + offset
- acceptance: Atomic ops compile to correct WASM bytecode; shared memory programs work

title: Update compiler design for codegen status and runtime count

IR_Method_Call, IR_Handle, IR_Perform still emit Unreachable (by design — lowered away by effect_lower). Runtime function count is now 17 (was 6). Atomic IR nodes exist but emit Unreachable. camp_worker_entry export exists.

title: Update effects design for 4-byte evidence slots
description:
- type: chore
- priority: 2
- labels: docs,effects
- description: |
    The effects design (openspec/specs/effects/design.md) specifies 8-byte evidence record slots (fn_idx + env_ptr). The implementation uses 4-byte slots storing a closure pointer directly, then loading fn_idx and env from within the closure at dispatch time. The design doc should reflect this optimization.
- acceptance: effects/design.md documents 4-byte evidence slots with closure pointer layout

title: Implement $ mutable variable semantics
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: parser,typecheck,codegen
- description: |
    `$`-prefixed variables are parsed but no mutation semantics are enforced. The spec says `$` variables can be reassigned within their scope but cannot be captured by closures (especially parallel closures).
- acceptance: $ variables can be reassigned; compiler prevents capture by closures

title: Structured concurrency warnings for unjoined spawns
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: typecheck,parallelism
- description: |
    The parallelism spec requires that every `Spawn.spawn!` must be followed by exactly one `Spawn.join!` or `Spawn.cancel!` before the handler exits. Currently there's no enforcement — unjoined spawns silently leak resources.
- design: |
    1. In typecheck, track spawned handles in a set within the handler scope
    2. On handler exit, check if any handles are unjoined
    3. Emit warning (future: error) for unjoined spawns
    4. Handler auto-cancels outstanding handles on exit
- acceptance: Compiler warns when a spawned handle is never joined or cancelled

title: Implement trait stdlib modules (Eq, Ord, Hash, Display, Clone)
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: stdlib,generics-traits
- description: |
    Core traits (Eq, Ord, Hash, Display, Clone) are specified but not implemented. These are needed for Map/Set keys, formatting, and comparison.
- acceptance: Eq/Ord/Hash/Display/Clone traits defined with implementations for primitive types

title: Handle(a) opacity and one-shot enforcement
description:
- type: feature
- priority: 2
- labels: typecheck,codegen,parallelism
- description: |
    Handle(a) is specified as opaque, one-shot, and move-semantics only. Currently it's just `i32` with no encapsulation. No runtime error on double-join. Cannot be passed to another spawned computation.
- design: |
    1. Type-level: Handle(a) should be a distinct type, not just i32
    2. Runtime: track handle state (Pending/Completed/Joined/Cancelled) in a handle table
    3. Double-join or double-cancel should trap
    4. Move semantics: after join/cancel, handle variable is consumed
- acceptance: Double-join traps at runtime; Handle cannot be used after consumption
